# Home Environment Manager v0.4.0 — International environmental intelligence

## A complete new public identity with backward compatibility

**Air Quality Advisor becomes Home Environment Manager.** The new name covers
real measured environmental conditions and the future direction toward optional
PID climate-device control. **PID is NOT implemented or enabled in this release.**

The internal Home Assistant domain remains `air_quality_advisor`, so existing
entities, sensors, configured areas, Lovelace dashboards, local measurement
history and the `air_quality_advisor.announce` service remain compatible.
A new `home_environment_manager.announce` alias invokes the same action
without duplicating notifications.
The existing `custom:air-quality-advisor-card` type continues to work; the
new `custom:home-environment-manager-card` name is available as an alias.

This release also includes a new vector product banner, updated architecture
diagram, expanded international setup documentation and six real-source Lovelace
screenshots (including scientific desktop and mobile examples).

## International, evidence-grounded capabilities

- Configurable per-provider **US EPA, European categorical and custom AQI**
  mapping: country, sensor units and index categories are never guessed.
- Additional real NO₂, O₃ and SO₂ sensor readings in normalized units, clearly
  separate from long-term and statutory exposure standards.
- Any Home Assistant provider's numeric **pollen** forecast, with explicit
  provider-scale configuration and opt-in high-pollen ventilation policy.
- Measured CO₂-window ventilation learning, conservative target-time estimates
  only with verified true CO₂ hardware and a stable decline.
- Air purifier particle CADR/room volume screening, extraction/moisture-event
  indications and descriptive indoor/outdoor particle ratios.
- Long-term radon observation with strict annual coverage gates; validated
  30-minute formaldehyde averages; calibrated A-weighted acoustic averages;
  bedtime noise exposure and daylight/spectral illuminance data when measured.
- Optional thermal comfort **ISO 7730:2025 PMV/PPD**, powered by a pinned,
  maintained `pythermalcomfort` dependency, withheld without all required
  physical measurements, clothing and activity settings.
- Measured overheating degree-hours, existing ASHRAE-inspired adaptive comfort,
  dew-point, humidity-ratio, surface condensation and time-weighted PM history.

**Important:** Sensor types and verification are not established merely by
an entity ID or the manufacturer's marketing. These are engineering
indicators, not medical advice or building certification; PMV/PPD,
exposure history and cooling opportunities are explicitly distinguished
from regulatory compliance.

## Configuration and privacy

A new clear **International air quality & pollen** settings page establishes
data-provider scales. A room selector opens three optional pages for airflow
and purifier measurements, verified specialist sensors and complete comfort
inputs. Unconfigured features remain unavailable rather than being filled
with invented estimates. No country, outdoor API, or extra cloud account is
required. Data comes from existing Home Assistant sensors and is processed
locally with a compact bounded history.

Weather and pollution guards, Announcement Hub's explicit `area` targeting,
the existing recommendation entity and persistent configuration survive
upgrade. No new automatic climate actuator is created or operated.

## Installation and verification

Update through HACS and restart Home Assistant so Python modules and the
bundled card refresh. The automated release pipeline checks Python tests,
all shipped translations, frontend rendering, JSON syntax, Hassfest and
HACS compliance before publishing. The optional time-history results need
fresh observations and will initially report insufficient coverage.

[Read the complete feature and setup documentation](https://github.com/Chreece/HA-Air-Quality-Advisor/blob/main/README.md).
